test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 25 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Water flows into a tank having the dimensions of its base given as 200 m × 150 m through a rectangular pipe having dimensions given as 1.5 m × 1.25 m @ 20 kmph. In what time (in minutes) will the water rise by 2 meters?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Time** = (Volume of tank) ÷ (Area of pipe cross-section × Speed of flow)

Total **Volume** required = 200 × 150 × 2 = 60,000 m³

**Flow rate** per hour = 1.5 × 1.25 × 20,000 = 37,500 m³/hr

Time (in hours) = 60,000 ÷ 37,500 = 1.6 hours

Time (in min) = 1.6 × 60 = 96 min

**∴ The correct answer is 96 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Tank** dimensions: Length = 200 m, Breadth = 150 m, Height of water rise = 2 m

**Pipe** dimensions: Width = 1.5 m, Depth = 1.25 m

**Speed** of water = 20 kmph = 20,000 m/hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68423fea2d60f1d53f008bfe66ab21e934b28b4995f99978e6dfb7b24860fc00.png] 

⇒ Volume of water required = Length × Breadth × Height

⇒ Volume = 200 × 150 × 2 = 60,000 m³

⇒ Area of **cross-section** of pipe = 1.5 × 1.25 = 1.875 m²

⇒ Speed of water in m/min = (20 × 1000) ÷ 60 = 1000 ÷ 3 m/min

⇒ Volume of water flowing per minute = Area × Speed

⇒ Flow rate = 1.875 × (1000 ÷ 3) = 625 m³/min

⇒ Time taken = Total Volume ÷ Flow rate per minute

⇒ Time = 60,000 ÷ 625 = 96 min

**∴ The correct answer is 96 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cuboid

The volume of a rectangular tank is given by Length × Breadth × Height (L × B × H).

Rate of Flow

The amount of water flowing through a pipe per unit time is Area of cross-section × Velocity of flow.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/min, multiply by (1000 ÷ 60) or 50 ÷ 3.</p
